newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Briton rejects new Romanian baby-smuggling charge.
newsitem.headline: Briton rejects new Romanian baby-smuggling charge.

text.p: A Briton accused of smuggling a 15-month-old baby out of Romania on Friday rejected separate charges of complicity in the illegal adoption of a second two-year-old girl.
"I'm not guilty of the charge," John Boast told a court in the Transylvanian town of Oradea, on tHungary.
Boast, 46, a self-described charity worker from Great Harwood in Lancashire, was first charged in February with smuggling a 15-month-old Romanian Gypsy girl to Britain.
He was arrested over a second case in May -- the alleged purchase for about $60 of a two-year-old girl who was taken out of Romania in June 1995.
Asked by the court why he had given money to the natural father of the second girl -- who turned up in Britain in the second half of 1995 -- Boast said:
"I met the man by simple coincidence. I gave him the money because I was leaving Romania and I knew I could not carry Romanian money over the border."
The court judge adjourned the hearing until November 5, granting a request by Boast's lawyer to provide a translator for the father of the second girl, a Hungarian-speaking Romanian Gypsy.
Boast faces up to five years in jail for the first offence and an additional three years on the second count if found guilty as charged.
Boast, freed last week from six-month police custody, declined to comment when he left the Oradea court on Friday.
Boast had been visiting Romania ferrying truckloads of aid after the 1989 revolution, when reports and film of abandoned babies living in gruesome orphanages stunned the world.
Thousands of babies were taken out of Romania before 1994, when the country stiffened adoption rules to fight its image as a baby farm for childless Westerners.

British couple Adrian and Bernadette Mooney were tried and convicted in 1994 for trying to smuggle a baby girl out of Romania. Their two-year jail sentence was suspended after President Ion Iliescu intervened.
